question: In case of first false start in a running event, the athlete(s) shall be ___________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**warned**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In case of a first false start in a running event, the athlete(s) shall be **warned**.
 
• If there is a **second false start by the same athlete, they will be disqualified.**
 
• The rule on false starts was changed in **2003 to try to reduce the number of false starts in races.**
 
• **Under the old rule, an athlete could false start twice without being disqualified.**
 
• However, this led to some races being delayed for long periods of time due to multiple false starts.
 
• The** new rule has been successful in reducing the number of false starts, and races are now able to start and finish more quickly.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sprints (or dashes) are **short-distance contests **in** athletics and track** and field.
 
• They are some of the** earliest recorded running contests**, appearing at the **Ancient Olympic Games.**
 
• The **100-meter, 200-meter, and 400-meter sprints** are the three sprints that are currently run at the modern **Summer Olympics and outdoor World Championships.**
 
• The** stadion race, a dash** from one end of the stadium to the other, was the sole event included in the first **13 iterations of the Ancient Olympic Games.**
 
• The **400-meter track,** which eventually became the norm for track and field, was introduced for the first time at the **1928 Olympics.**
